transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sanjay Rao (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (CISO - Praxis), Ethan Morales (Head of IT - Praxis), Priya Shah (Compliance Manager - Praxis)

Summary: quick posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 alignment, Trust Center access, control mapping and evidence collection, plus specifics around RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency and KMS / encryption options. Agreement to share reports and schedule a follow-up for controls mapping and sample audit logs.

Topics covered: SOC2 report access; ISO 27001 controls mapping; Trust Center walkthrough; RBAC and SAML/SSO; audit logs and retention; data residency (EU); KMS / BYOK; evidence collection for auditor requests; Dedicated vs Private deployment notes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thank you for joining, um we're gonna run through Redwood's SOC2 and ISO posture, and then we can pore into any specific controls you're worried about. Laura, do you want to kick off with your top priorities?
[00:08] Laura Kim: yeah thanks, Jordan. our auditors asked for a high level mapping first — so we need the SOC 2 Type II, evidence of controls, and then a mapping to ISO 27001 clauses. also data residency, especially eu jurisdiction for some PHI-adjacent logs, and how key management works if we use hosted vs private.
[00:26] Jordan Lee: yep makes sense. Sanjay will walk through the technical bits, I'll cover the compliance artifacts and the trust center access.
[00:31] Sanjay Rao: hey, quick note — I'm gonna be a little granular on audit logs and RBAC, so maybe crosstalk is fine.
[00:36] Ethan Morales: quick clarification — by "audit logs" do you mean admin actions and user-level activity or token-level request logs? we need both for our review.
[00:44] Sanjay Rao: good question. Redwood keeps several tiers: admin/console audit, API request logs (per-request metadata), and token-level usage metadata. request logs can be exported to your S3 or to syslog, depending on the setup.
[00:55] Priya Shah: and retention? our policy expects 365-day retention for some categories.
[00:59] Jordan Lee: default retention on hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated or Private we can support longer retention or ship logs to your account for indefinite retention — we can also stream to your SIEM.
[01:12] Laura Kim: okay, that matters. also need to see how RBAC maps to our least-privilege roles, and SAML SSO for console access.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: we support SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning, role-mapping from your IdP. RBAC in the console has admin, devops, observer roles; we can do custom roles for Dedicated/Private customers.
[01:28] Ethan Morales: on KMS — do you do BYOK or is it Redwood-managed keys? our preference is BYOK via AWS KMS or HSM.
[01:36] Sanjay Rao: Redwood supports both: Redwood-managed KMS for hosted, and customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Dedicated/Private, typically via your AWS KMS or cloud HSM. rotation, access policies, and logs are available. a note: some of the UI labels in our docs say "K-M-S" spelled out, sometimes transcribed funny in older docs.
[01:52] Priya Shah: for ISO mapping, do you provide a controls matrix already?
[01:56] Jordan Lee: yes we have a controls matrix that maps SOC 2 controls to ISO 27001 clauses and to Redwood features/evidence buckets. i'll share the matrix and the SOC2 Type II report after the call.
[02:05] Laura Kim: will that include evidence samples? like screenshots of RBAC settings, SSO config, audit log exports?
[02:11] Jordan Lee: we can include redacted screenshots and examples of log formats; but for full raw logs we'll do a sample export via the SE.
[02:17] Ethan Morales: what about penetration testing and vulnerability scanning reports?
[02:21] Jordan Lee: we publish a summary in the trust center; we can provide the attestation letters and scan summaries. full pentest reports are typically shared under NDA for enterprise customers — we can open that if needed.
[02:32] Priya Shah: do you have SOC 2 Type II right now? what date range?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: yes, current SOC 2 Type II for the period ending Dec 31, 2025. we'll send the PDF.
[02:41] Laura Kim: great — auditors will want the auditor firm name and scope included.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: sure, we'll include auditor and scope metadata.
[02:48] Sanjay Rao: digging into logs — export formats are JSON lines with a few common fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id, action, resource, src_ip. we also capture KV cache ops for inference if you enable KV logging, but that's optional and can be disabled.
[03:10] Ethan Morales: KV cache ops — can that include model prompt content? we need to avoid storing PHI.
[03:15] Sanjay Rao: default is not to persist full prompts in audit logs; we have options: redact or don't log payloads. for healthcare customers we recommend Private or Dedicated with strict logging.
[03:27] Laura Kim: and data residency — we have EU data residency requirements for patient metadata. how do you guarantee region isolation?
[03:33] Jordan Lee: hosted deployments can be pinned to region clusters; Dedicated gives you a dedicated pool in a chosen region; Private can be fully within your VPC or on-prem. for EU residency we can provision a Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 or a Private deployment with your controls.
[03:47] Priya Shah: auditability: auditors will ask for change history for roles and IAM. does Redwood maintain history for user role changes?
[03:53] Sanjay Rao: yes, console admin audit tracks changes to users/roles with timestamps and the actor. retention follows the same policy, but we can export to your log store for longer-term retention.
[04:03] Ethan Morales: can we integrate with our SIEM? we use Splunk and Datadog.
[04:06] Sanjay Rao: absolutely — we have native sinks for Datadog and a Splunk HEC endpoint; we can forward logs in near-real time.
[04:11] Laura Kim: one more on KMS: key rotation proof. auditors want to see rotation schedule and evidence of encryption in transit and at rest.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; at rest keys are KMS-backed; rotation logs come from KMS — we can surface the rotation events and provide a sample audit.
[04:27] Priya Shah: and for ISO 27001 evidence mapping — do you have a mapping that shows which Redwood artifact satisfies which control?
[04:33] Jordan Lee: yes, that's the controls matrix I mentioned — I'll attach a mapping that has the control, the Redwood artifact (e.g., SOC 2 test, policy doc, screenshot) and a recommended evidence sample.
[04:41] Ethan Morales: about privileged access — do you support just-in-time (JIT) for elevated roles or MFA enforcement?
[04:47] Sanjay Rao: currently we enforce MFA for all admin console access and support role-based scopes; JIT is not a first-class feature yet but we can enable temporary elevated keys using our sessions API in Dedicated/Private through your identity provider.
[04:59] Laura Kim: any third-party subprocessors or vendors we should flag?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: yes we have a subprocessor list, includes cloud provider, monitoring vendor, telemetry/analytics provider — we'll share the current list.
[05:10] Priya Shah: about evidence collection for the auditors — who will own getting the screenshots and exports?
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Jordan + Sanjay will provide sample screenshots and run the export; we'll label the items for auditor consumption.
[05:21] Ethan Morales: if we go Dedicated, what is the onboarding timeline for evidence collection?
[05:26] Jordan Lee: provisioning Dedicated typically takes 4-6 weeks; but for the compliance review we can provide the SOC2 artifacts and control matrix immediately, and partial evidence via screenshots. full environment-level evidence would follow deployment.
[05:37] Laura Kim: that works. auditors usually want a view of change management too; do you have a CM system or ticketing records?
[05:43] Sanjay Rao: we can provide a redacted sample of change records, postmortems, and release notes that map to controls.
[05:50] Priya Shah: any gotchas with SSO/SCIM provisioning? we've had issues in the past with group sync frequency and stale roles.
[05:56] Jordan Lee: sync frequency is configurable; by default it's incremental and every 15 minutes. we can bump frequency or use on-demand sync for critical groups.
[06:04] Ethan Morales: what about network-level controls — do you support IP allowlists for management plane?
[06:09] Sanjay Rao: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support management plane IP allowlists; hosted customers can use organization-wide allowlists and MFA to harden access.
[06:18] Laura Kim: ok, let's talk about the Trust Center access — how will we get in?
[06:22] Jordan Lee: i'll send a Trust Center link and provision a read-only token for your team. it has the SOC reports, policies, and attestation artifacts. if you need deeper artefacts we'll request a short NDA and provide extra docs.
[06:33] Priya Shah: perfect. add me and Laura on that.
[06:36] Jordan Lee: noted.
[06:38] (brief crosstalk)
[06:42] Jordan Lee: any blockers from Praxis side for that?
[06:45] Laura Kim: none, just need the files and the mapping. also can you indicate evidence for backup/restore controls?
[06:52] Sanjay Rao: backups are encrypted and stored in region; we have snapshot schedules and can provide retention and restore test logs as evidence.
[07:02] Ethan Morales: good. last item — can you show us an example of an audit log export now or is that in follow-up?
[07:07] Sanjay Rao: follow-up — i'll run a sample export after the call and share a sanitized JSON lines file via secure link.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: okay, recap and next steps: we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and controls matrix, provision Trust Center access, SE will run log export and provide sample screenshots, and we'll schedule a controls mapping session week of Apr 12.
[07:28] Laura Kim: sounds good, thank you.
[07:31] Priya Shah: thanks everyone.
[07:33] Ethan Morales: appreciate it.
[07:35] Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items.

End of transcript.
